name: Proxemics
citation: Hall, E.T. (1966). The hidden dimension. Anchor Books.
rejection_rationale: Collapses into Privacy Regulation (Altman) + Spatial Navigation (SN framework). Hall's four distance zones (intimate, personal, social, public) are fully explained by IC interoceptive boundary management + SN peripersonal space coding. No independent T1.5 residual remains after this decomposition.
key_references: Hall, E.T. (1966). The hidden dimension. Anchor Books.

function_form.function_form: Zone(d, ψ) = {intimate: d<0.45m, personal: 0.45-1.2m, social: 1.2-3.6m, public: >3.6m} · κ(culture)

variables.\u03ba(culture): Cultural scaling factor (contact vs non-contact culture)

predictions: Japanese social distance ~15% larger than US (non-contact culture offset)
Latin American intimate zone ~30% smaller than Northern European
